description:
FILED s529a (Opus agent, 2026-10-31) while fixing #3824.  PRE-EXISTING for the variable-copy spelling; the element spellings were right on main only BY the #3824 alias.

A re-bless of an ARRAY / CODE (non-hash) referent through ONE copy of the reference is not seen through another copy.  perl blesses the REFERENT, so every reference to it sees the new class.

REPRO (scratch/s529a/pr/b1.pl rows 11 21 22 24):
    my $o3 = bless [], 'K'; my @c = ($o3); bless $o3, 'Other'; print ref($c[0]), "\n";   # perl Other
    my $od = bless [], 'K'; my $re = $od; bless $od, 'Other'; print ref($re), "\n";       # perl Other
    my $oe = bless [], 'K'; my @ce = ($oe); bless $ce[0], 'Other'; print ref($oe), "\n";  # perl Other
    my $og = bless [], 'K'; my %hg = (a => $og); bless $og, 'O2'; print ref($hg{a}), "\n"; # perl O2
  PCL (after #3824): K / K / K / K.  A HASH referent is right in every spelling (its class is the
  :__class__ key of the table itself).

MECHANISM: p-bless's array/code arm writes the class on the BOX it was handed (the variable or a
copy), and box-set / %p-container-snapshot copy that slot into every new container -- the slot is
both the cache and, for a raw vector / function payload, the ONLY record (ir-spec §2.6 "Array/code/glob
refs keep the class on the wrapper box").  Before #3824 the array construction arm stored the
VARIABLE's box itself, so rows 11 and 22 were right by aliasing (and `$c[0] = 3` rewrote $o3).

SHAPE TO MEASURE: a weak eq table referent -> class for vector / function payloads (the
*p-handle-stash* / *p-sv-stash* precedent: a count test keeps it off the hot path), written by
p-bless, read FIRST by %p-target-class; every reader that reads (p-box-class obj) directly as a
fast "is this an object" check must be audited (method dispatch, overload lookup) -- they would read
the stale cache.  Measure first how many direct slot readers there are.
subject: a re-bless of an ARRAY / CODE referent through one copy of the reference is not seen through another (the class of a non-hash referent lives on each container)
